children: TOKYO, October 8 (Reuters) - Foreign investors turned netbuyers of Japanese stocks for the week ending on October 3, capital flows data showed on Thursday.    Foreigners bought a net 2,191.9 billion yen worth of shares inthe week through Oct. 3, after selling a net 354.2 billion yenin the week before that.    Japanese investors sold a net 347.6 billion yen of foreignbonds in the latest week after selling a net 682.3 billion yenthe week before.    Details of net investments were as follows (in billion yen):

FOREIGN INVESTMENT IN JAPAN:    (net)                                       stocks         bonds        bills    September 27 - October 3         +2,191.9        +585.7       -238.5     September 20 - September 26        -354.2r     -1,341.8     -3,267.2
JAPANESE INVESTMENT ABROAD:    (net; a minus sign indicates net selling and inflows of funds into Japan)

stocks         bonds        bills    September 27 - October 3         +1,324.6        -347.6       -156.0     September 20 - September 26        +225.8        -682.3r      +131.5r    September 13 - September 19         +44.3      -1,904.9       +347.1r    September 6  - September 12        +156.4r     +1,091.0       +150.8     August 30 - September 5            -478.8        +118.9r      +107.1

Notes:    - An "r" denotes a revised figure.    - Bonds include beneficiary certificates.    - Figures are based on contracts and are rounded.    - The MOF's capital flows data can be found in English at:    http://www.mof.go.jp/international_policy/reference/itn_transactions_in_securities/week.pdf
